prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1367; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the claimant, who reports a low-speed collision in a parking lot and a wrist fracture from the impact. The claimant is not represented by an attorney and has been asked to send photos and the police report reference.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver is listed as a named insured on the policy in force at the time. Vehicle damage photos received; the rear bumper and tail light damage appears consistent with the described impact.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant again and the account of the incident matched the first call in every detail. The police report and two parties on scene confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time. No independent witnesses have come forward.

Entry 4: Medical records show a wrist fracture with a treatment course that followed a typical pattern, with physical therapy tapering as the claimant improved. The injury appears consistent with the kind and force of this type of collision. Records also note a small strain to the same area several years ago that healed fully.

Entry 5: A neighbor contacted the office and believes the vehicle already had damage a few weeks before the claimed date of loss. No earlier damage to the vehicle is recorded in our files, and the neighbor's statement has not yet been verified.

Entry 6: Photos confirm several details of the scene and damage, though they do not resolve the timing question raised by the neighbor. Next steps are to request the vehicle's prior repair history and a follow-up statement from the neighbor before making a coverage decision.
